section.form_description: The narrator on their feet in a crowded room, speaking about someone who has died. Sections are the things there are to say about the dead — a habit, a fight, a debt, the once they were wrong, the once they were right when it counted. The tone swings: a story that gets a laugh, a line that lands angry, a stretch that can barely be got through. What holds it together is that none of it is polite — every word is meant.
section.form_note: Eulogy, as named: nine people on their feet in the Normandy mess a few weeks after London, ryncol and his playlists going, each saying what there is to say about Thomas, each turn picking up the one before. This is a fork of the approved 2026-10-13 Jack-branch eulogy onto the Tali-romance branch (subject thomas.tali; config/narrators/thomas.tali.notes.md is the only ground truth, and it wins over todo15.10.26 and the old outline wherever they differ). The old structure is kept: same room, same ten-turn chain, the same speakers after the opener, the strongest beats where the Tali notes allow them (Joker's ratings, Kaidan's coup payoff, Grunt guarding the kitchen, Wrex's pyjak, EDI's clover). What changes: Tali opens and closes as the partner, and Jack drops to a friend's ~900 words in second place; Jack's romance beats (poems, 'I love you', the recording, Grissom long-distance, the no-promises rule) move to Tali in their Tali-notes form; Joker's name for the couple is now 'the Help Desk'. The todo review is applied as hard rules in the promises: no canon recaps (a canon event appears only at the moment Thomas walks into it); nobody outs him (Tali alone breaks the silence about his hands, on purpose; Joker swallows the hospital line and never opens the log; EDI declines to read the medical file; the mother story is Liara's alone); one owner per trait ('handyman first, cooking second', 'joked about his hands first' and the locker count are Tali's, 'outdrank everyone' and the ratings Joker's, Kropotkin by name Liara's, the body on its way to Rouen Wrex's, the Akuze/Shepard origin Tali's closing turn); each flaw told by the person it cost; one mirrored wound per speaker. The devices (what someone gave him, their playlist, a habit of his now theirs, 'Shepard is missing') are a pool, not a per-turn checklist: each lands in a few turns only, unannounced, as assigned in the promises (voice-check feedback 2026-11-11). Turns are rough talk at a wake, not composed speeches; at most two refusals in the whole episode (Joker's swallowed line, EDI's medical file); nobody knows the evening's structure. Tali's collapse is saved for the last turn: in her first she nearly breaks and swallows it. Spine is mixed: Thomas is not in the corpus, so sections anchor on the occasions his notes place him in and the speaker's own vantage on them. Canon: genophage cured, Wrex leads, geth-quarian peace with Legion dead, Mordin and Thane dead, Grunt alive, Tali and Garrus evacuated from the conduit run; the crew do not know there was a choice, only its consequences, and Shepard is missing, not confirmed dead. Shepard-Thomas material is limited to what the speaker could have witnessed or been told. Ten sections, inside the form's 6-14. target_words was pinned by the user at 17,690 and raised to 17,940 for the armor-straps beat (above the form's clamp, as the brief's 45-60 minutes asks). Turn sizes follow the brief rather than an even voice balance: Tali 3,000 + 3,600, Jack 900, and Jack's freed words spread across the other seven (Joker 1,900, Kaidan 1,850, Liara 1,700, EDI 1,690, James 1,300, Wrex 1,150, Grunt 850). Handoffs: Tali's swallowed 'give me a second' to Jack covering for her; Jack's 'too good for him' to Joker's Help Desk; Joker's swallowed line to Liara on what he never said aloud; Liara's careful words to Grunt's 'same tank'; Grunt's rating of his strength to James's punch; James's eggs to Kaidan's pill cases; Kaidan's coup voice to Wrex being told he was wrong; Wrex's 'you show up' to EDI's eleven tasks; EDI's files to the one file she does not have, which Tali carries in a sealed pouch.

promises: James takes Grunt's rating of Thomas as no fighter and agrees, then tells the one punch: a Terra Firma type told a turian waitress humanity should have finished the job at Shanxi, Thomas gave one quiet warning, the man said it again. Thumb inside the fist, the man went down mostly from surprise. After, on the curb with ice on his hand, shaking worse than ever, 'bad even at this', and the guilt. James was there; this is the snap, told once

Vancouver, the part James witnessed as the guard: Thomas came every week to see Shepard and lost at chess every week. Nothing about what they said; only what a guard could see. No separate 'Shepard is missing' beat, no Akuze retelling

The mirrored wound: offered N7, James did not think he had earned it; Thomas listed every reason he was the right man, and when James asked if that went for Thomas too, he changed the subject to eggs ('seven, for courage'). What James gave him: asked if he was built for the line, James said no and taught him to stand anyway; whether he took it. 'Tembleque' and 'seismic event' only lightly (Tali has the hands)

Picking up Grunt's straps: the last time James saw him. Thomas suiting up before London with his last playlist on loud, Grunt and James on the straps, and on the last tracks (Gasolina, then Killing in the Name) all three of them jumping in half-done armor. James tells only what he saw and heard: a man who had made up his mind and was happy about it. This is where 'taught him to stand anyway' pays off; James does not know whether that was taking it or saying goodbye. He does not list the playlist (EDI has the file) and quotes no lyrics

The dead hang Thomas won with a Wrex joke and called a fluke for a month, the limericks and the towel during his pull-ups, asking Cortez what Robert was like. No playlist and no habit beat in this turn. No Omega, Vancouver-invasion or Fehl Prime recap. This is a eulogy: lament, how they bonded, what he loved, celebration

required_facts.fact: Days after the destruction of the Bahak system's Alpha Relay, the galaxy is in turmoil over Commander Shepard's alleged role in the deaths of over 300,000 batarians. The Citadel Council publicly denounces Shepard, Alliance Councilor Donnel Udina works to deflect blame away from the Systems Alliance, and the Batarian Hegemony demands that Shepard be handed over for retribution. Shepard, having surrendered to Alliance authority, is confined and awaiting trial on Earth while the Normandy SR-2 is impounded and stripped of its Cerberus upgrades. On Omega, Alliance marine Lieutenant James Vega is drinking and playing cards in a bar, watching a newscast about the uproar over Shepard. Frustrated, he tears the screen from the wall and offers the krogan bartender payment for the damage. The batarians he had been playing cards with brand him a "Shepard Lover" and attack him; Vega fights the whole group off, smashing one man with the torn-out screen and crashing through a window with another. Admiral David Anderson arrives on Omega with a squad of soldiers and tells Vega he is being brought in for additional training. In an aircar on final approach to the docked Normandy SR-2, Anderson presses Vega to move past "the incident on Fehl Prime" and become the soldier the Alliance expects him to be. Vega, still carrying guilt over that mission, demands to be thrown in the brig instead. Anderson reveals that Vega will in fact be guarding the brig, and that it holds one very specific prisoner: Commander Shepard. The assignment places Vega aboard the Normandy and in Shepard's orbit just before the Reapers strike Earth, explaining his presence as a squadmate at the start of Mass Effect 3. A single omniscient narration panel in the comic assumes Shepard personally destroyed the Bahak relay; players who did not complete the Arrival mission may instead be told Alliance marines were responsible.

Vega is posted aboard the impounded Normandy SR-2 as guard over the detained Shepard

As Commander Shepard's fame grew following the appointment as the first human Spectre, political groups on the Citadel sought the Commander's endorsement and support. Charles Saracino, the charismatic leader of the Terra Firma Party—a growing political movement advocating for human independence and resistance to alien influence—sought Shepard's backing for his run for a seat in the Alliance Parliament. Outside Flux in the Upper Wards, Saracino and his supporters gathered near the stairs, promoting his candidacy and xenophobic rhetoric. Saracino approached Shepard directly, believing that a public endorsement from the first human Spectre would be invaluable to his political ambitions. Shepard faced a critical choice: endorse Saracino's candidacy or refuse to support the party. Squad members in Shepard's presence voiced their own objections to Saracino's platform. Ashley Williams, if present, expressed her own concerns about his approach. Kaidan Alenko, Liara T'Soni, Garrus Vakarian, and Urdnot Wrex all had varying reactions to Saracino's xenophobic stance. Shepard could encourage or curtail these objections, further shaping the political landscape. Per choice conditional: - Endorsed Saracino: Granted Renegade points; Saracino gained parliamentary support, strengthening Terra Firma's political position - Refused endorsement: Granted Paragon points; Saracino was later exposed and pleaded guilty to tax evasion (in Legendary Edition) In Mass Effect 2, news reports reflected Shepard's choice. If endorsed, Terra Firma gained significant parliamentary influence, creating a political faction that viewed Shepard with approval. If not endorsed, Saracino faced legal consequences, and Terra Firma's growth was stalled. Despite the legal outcome, the party continued to exist as a political force with xenophobic elements. The choice represented a fundamental decision about how Shepard's influence would be used in human politics and foreshadowed the deeper tensions between human unity and xenophobic isolationism that would surface in later conflicts.

During the First Contact War, Lieutenant Abrudas commanded a turian squad that discovered a downed turian research vessel on the human colony world Shanxi. Her commanding officer, General Desolas Arterius, sent her a false message to rendezvous with him. Abrudas fell into a trap orchestrated by human mercenaries including Jack Harper, Ben Hislop, and Eva Coré, who were searching for an alien artifact the turians were attempting to recover. Acting on the fake message, Abrudas led her soldiers into ambush and unwittingly revealed the location of the downed research vessel to the human mercenaries. This incident was part of the larger First Contact War conflict as humans and turians came into contact for the first time. The event is detailed in the Mass Effect: Evolution comic series and serves as a prelude to the larger struggle between humans and turians that would define humanity's early interactions with the galactic community. The exact artifact that both forces were seeking later proved to be the Arca Monolith, which possessed reality-altering properties and would become central to Desolas' attempted coup on the turian homeworld of Palaven.
Human mercenaries discover location of crashed turian research vessel
Sets in motion the larger First Contact War conflict
Leads to Desolas' subsequent pursuit of the Arca Monolith and attempted coup

canon.statement: In the first weeks after the war, Shepard's death is not confirmed to the crew. Anderson never saw him on the station. The Normandy crash-landed, there's been no word, and the crew takes that silence to mean he's dead: there's no body and no report. After a few months, Shepard is held to be dead by everyone, the crew included: the rubble has been cleared, what the Crucible did is better understood, and there was nowhere on the station he could have escaped to. There is still no body, so no burial. Shepard's lover puts his name on the Normandy's memorial wall, or chooses not to, and the crew holds a night of remembrance for him: to celebrate the man he was, to mourn him, or both.

scenes.title: Anderson Stays Behind as the Normandy Leaves Earth
scenes.when: 2186, Vancouver, Earth, the first hours of the Reaper invasion (Prologue: Earth)
scenes.where: a Systems Alliance HQ tower in Vancouver, then the ruined streets and spaceport, then the Normandy SR-2 shuttle bay

beats.text: Six months after Bahak, Shepard was under arrest and relieved of command in Vancouver. Anderson escorted the Commander, with Lieutenant James Vega, into a Systems Alliance defense committee meeting, where Shepard confirmed the committee's fear that the Reapers had returned and were coming for Earth. Contact was lost with Luna Base mid-meeting; a Reaper capital ship then descended over the city and blasted the tower, killing the committee and staff. Only Shepard and Anderson walked out.

Anderson handed Shepard an M-3 Predator pistol and the two crossed the rooftops of burning Vancouver while Oculi tore Alliance fighters apart overhead. They raised the Virmire survivor — Ashley Williams or Kaidan Alenko — by radio and told them to get to the Normandy. Along the way Shepard saw a child alone, who refused help and fled into a building; Shepard fought husks hand to hand and, further on, the war's first Cannibals beside two Alliance soldiers, then reached a comm unit by a crashed gunship and hailed the Normandy, which bombed the area clear.

As Shepard moved to board, Anderson refused to leave — a million more survivors like the men behind them needed a leader — and stayed on Earth to raise a resistance. He threw Shepard the dog tags that reinstated the Commander in the Alliance and charged Shepard with bringing back help from the Council. Shepard protested; Anderson did not change his mind.

From the lifting Normandy Shepard watched the same child climb into an evac Kodiak. A Reaper Destroyer rose over the buildings and shot the shuttle down, killing everyone aboard, the boy included. Shepard stepped back from the open bay doors as the ship cleared Vancouver past the burning wreckage of the human fleets.

Aboard ship, James Vega was incredulous that Shepard meant to follow Anderson's order and leave Earth to beg the Council for aid; the argument allowed a Paragon or Renegade interrupt. Admiral Hackett then contacted Shepard by comm and assigned the next mission, Priority: Mars.

scenes.title: Sparring with Vega in the Shuttle Bay
scenes.when: 2186, during the war, the first time Shepard comes down to the shuttle bay
scenes.where: the Normandy SR-2 shuttle bay, by the weapons bench and the overhead bars

beats.text: Vega keeps to the shuttle bay, by a weapons bench, trading banter with his friend Steve Cortez between missions. The first time Shepard comes down, James is doing pull-ups on the overhead bars. His greeting scales to how long Shepard took to visit: soon after Garrus comes aboard he just takes Shepard's word about the turian because he can't tell them apart; if EDI has a body he asks whether Shepard is "shitting" him; if Shepard left it a long time he wonders aloud what the Commander is doing below decks with the "grunts," or asks whether they took a wrong turn at the elevator.
However the first meeting goes, they end up in a sparring match. If Shepard put the visit off for a long time, James promises to go easy, "just in case."

Mid-spar, James gives the short version of his life before the Normandy. His old CO, Captain Toni — a hard-assed son of a bitch but a good leader — was killed with most of James's squad while they were protecting a civilian colony, Fehl Prime, from a Collector attack.

With Toni dead, command fell to James. He had to choose between saving the colony or saving the intel his squad had recovered — intel that could be used to destroy the Collectors. He saved the intel and let the colony fall, then learned too late that Shepard had wiped out the Collectors without it. The colony died for nothing, and that is the guilt he carries into the war.

scenes.title: Vega Decorated for Fehl Prime
scenes.when: 2185, Citadel (Mass Effect: Paragon Lost), after the Collector attack on Fehl Prime

beats.text: On the Citadel, Anderson and Admiral Hackett commend Lieutenant James Vega for Fehl Prime. They tell him the intel he chose to save — pulling out Treeya instead of the colonists — could give the Alliance a short-term edge on the Collectors, an antidote to their Seeker swarms, and new weapons and ship research.

Hackett pins a medal on Vega and promotes him to Lieutenant Commander. Anderson, seeing how hard Vega works to follow in Shepard's footsteps, tells him rumors of the Commander's death are premature and he may get to serve with Shepard one day, then hands him orders to report for N7 training.

Vega, Milque and Treeya return to Fehl Prime while the Alliance sifts the wreckage. Finding April's ruined stuffed animal, Vega breaks down and runs through the ruins; the others catch up with him at the monument raised to the lost colonists, and he resolves to make their deaths mean something.

scenes.title: Saracino Seeks Shepard's Endorsement at the Terra Firma Protest
scenes.when: 2183, Citadel, after Sovereign's attack, during shore leave
scenes.where: Upper Wards of the Citadel, near the stairs by Flux

beats.text: After Captain Anderson summons Shepard to meet him at Flux, a Terra Firma party protest is found gathered on the Citadel Upper Wards near Flux, a group of people chanting slogans against alien influence on humanity. Charles Saracino, the current leader of Terra Firma, stands at the front of the group and calls Shepard over for a conversation.

Whichever squadmates Shepard brought have their own reactions to Saracino. If Ashley Williams is present she voices her own objections to him, which Shepard can encourage or curtail; Kaidan Alenko, Liara T'Soni, Garrus Vakarian, and Urdnot Wrex each have their own complaints to make as well.

Saracino, a vehement critic of the Alliance's policy toward alien races, believes humanity should resist alien influences by any means necessary—even militarily in the worst case. He is running for a political office in the Alliance Parliament and considers the support of the first human Spectre invaluable.

Saracino asks Shepard to endorse him for a seat in the Alliance parliament. Shepard can agree or refuse the endorsement, possibly believing it would be unwise or that humans need to cooperate with alien races instead. Even if Shepard refuses, Saracino asks whether Shepard would at least make a public statement of support for his candidacy.

If Shepard endorses Saracino's candidacy, the Commander earns Renegade points and Saracino is grateful for Shepard's respect of the democratic process. He returns to the protest satisfied. Cut news reports, restored in Legendary Edition, later show the Terra Firma Party gaining support in Parliament.

If Shepard refuses to endorse Saracino, the Commander earns Paragon points. Saracino is still grateful for Shepard's respect of the democratic process despite the rejection and returns to the protest. Cut news reports, restored in Legendary Edition, later show Saracino pleading guilty to tax evasion.

evidence.text:
Terra Firma was a human political party that opposed humanity's growing integration into the galactic community, holding that humanity needed to stand alone to remain strong. Members cited Shanxi and the First Contact War as proof that aliens could not be trusted, marked Armistice Day with an annual protest, and opposed the teaching of alien languages in schools. The party was founded after first contact with the turians, when humans learned how many races made up Citadel space, out of genuine concern that human individuality might be diluted. Its manifesto was not especially extremist, but it attracted xenophobes and reactionaries, and it declined to curb its members' racist rhetoric on free-speech grounds.

In Mass Effect: Ascension (2173), Terra Firma was caught in a kickback scandal involving Nashan Stellar Dynamics, forcing party leader Inez Simmons to resign. Leadership candidates Charles Saracino and Claude Menneau campaigned vigorously; Menneau led the polls by three points until he vanished en route to a rally on Shanxi, his ship and crew never found. With his rival gone, Saracino ran unopposed and was elected party leader.

In Mass Effect, Commander Shepard could discuss the party with Ashley Williams aboard the Normandy; uncomfortable around aliens herself, Ashley reacted angrily to comparisons with Terra Firma, calling its members jackals who had strayed from the founders' ideals. Shepard could also encounter a Terra Firma protest on the Citadel led by Saracino himself during the assignment Citadel: Our Own Worst Enemy, where Saracino, seeking a political seat, asked Shepard to endorse him. "Terra firma" is Latin for "solid Earth." A Shadow Broker dossier later listed the Illusive Man's liaisons Staci and Stephi Strong as the "Terra Firma Twins."

Charles Saracino of the Terra Firma Party approached you on the Citadel, seeking support in the next election. You declined. *Alternative journal entry:* Charles Saracino of the Terra Firma Party approached you on the Citadel, seeking support in the next election. You said you would endorse him publically. *Alternative journal entry:* Charles Saracino of the Terra Firma Party approached you on the Citadel, seeking support in the next election. You said you would vote for him.

**Nashan Stellar Dynamics** is a human corporation that makes parts for starships. In 2173, the political party Terra Firma was involved in a kickback scandal with Nashan Stellar Dynamics. The political fallout was immense and forced the leader of Terra Firma, Inez Simmons, to step down from her position. The company also manufactured T6\-FBA Couplings. This model of couplings was eventually discontinued prior to 2185, but obtaining a set of them proves central to the engineers' maintenance work on the Normandy SR\-2.

Terra Firma is an Alliance political party formed after the First Contact War. Its policy agenda is based on the principle that Earth must 'stand firm' against alien influences. This covers a variety of legislation. Recent activities by Terra Firma include opposition to a law requiring high school alien language study, a proposal to increase tariffs on alien imports, and leading a popular movement to mark the First Contact War with a public holiday. Though founded by well\-meaning individuals who feared the submersion of native human cultures under a wave of 'alien vogue', Terra Firma's agenda attracts many jingoists and xenophobes.

evidence.text: Saracino Seeks Shepard's Endorsement at the Terra Firma Protest. 2183, Citadel, after Sovereign's attack, during shore leave Upper Wards of the Citadel, near the stairs by Flux If Shepard endorses Saracino's candidacy, the Commander earns Renegade points and Saracino is grateful for Shepard's respect of the democratic process. He returns to the protest satisfied. Cut news reports, restored in Legendary Edition, later show the Terra Firma Party gaining support in Parliament.

**Terra Firma** is a human political party who opposes humanity's growing integration into the galactic community. The members believe humanity needs to stand alone if they are to remain strong. They cite Shanxi and the First Contact War as examples of why humans can't trust aliens, and mark Armistice Day with a protest every year. Part of their platform involves opposing the teaching of alien languages in schools. Terra Firma was founded after contact was made with the turians, and humans became aware of just how many races comprised Citadel space. The party was created in response to a genuine concern that humanity's individuality might be diluted or lost after too much integration into alien cultures. The party's manifesto isn't particularly extremist, but they tend to be a magnet for xenophobes and reactionaries, and the party does nothing to curtail the racist comments of its members, under the pretext that the party will not abridge its members' freedom of speech. |  | ***“Salvation comes with a cost.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Ascension** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

Charles Saracino was the head of the Terra Firma party. Commander Shepard met him on the Upper Wards of the Citadel, where he was taking part in a Terra Firma protest marking Armistice Day, the anniversary of the end of the First Contact War. Like most members of Terra Firma, Saracino believed Earth must stand firm against alien influences "politically, socially, and in the worst case, militarily," and cited Shanxi as an episode humanity should never forget when dealing with alien races. If Urdnot Wrex, Garrus Vakarian, Ashley Williams or Liara T'Soni were in Shepard's party without another human squadmate present, one of them ended up arguing with Saracino and Shepard had to intervene.

Saracino was seeking one of the "spacer" seats in the Alliance parliament at Arcturus Station, but ran into a problem with the eligibility rules: to vote for a spacer candidate, a citizen had to spend more than six months a year in space while never remaining in any settled system for more than a month. Shepard fit those conditions, so Saracino asked whether the Commander would be interested in voting for him.

In Mass Effect: Ascension, set in 2183 after the Battle of the Citadel, Paul Grayson reminisced about his first kill, Keo, one of the bodyguards of Claude Menneau, who had been Saracino's chief rival. The Illusive Man had Menneau assassinated, believing Saracino would be easier to influence.

In 2185, if Shepard had endorsed his candidacy, a news report quoted Saracino as pleased that Terra Firma had gained seats in a recent parliamentary election and promising continuing pro-human changes. If Shepard had refused to endorse him, a report instead stated that Saracino had been charged with tax evasion, had pled guilty, and was awaiting sentencing. These Mass Effect 2 news reports were cut from the game's original release and restored in Mass Effect Legendary Edition.

Citadel: Our Own Worst Enemy was a Mass Effect assignment available after Race Against Time: Sovereign. After Captain Anderson summoned Commander Shepard to meet him at Flux, a group of people chanting slogans gathered in the Upper Wards near the stairs by Flux, where the player first encountered Emily Wong. At the front stood Charles Saracino, current leader of the Terra Firma Party and a vehement critic of the Alliance's policy toward alien races, who believed humanity should resist alien influences by any means necessary, even militarily in the worst case. Saracino was running for a seat in the Alliance Parliament and considered the support of the first human Spectre invaluable.

If Ashley Williams was in the party she voiced her own objections to Saracino, which Shepard could encourage or curtail; Kaidan Alenko, Liara T'Soni, Garrus Vakarian, and Urdnot Wrex also had their own complaints. Conversation with Saracino provided information about Terra Firma, Shanxi, and the First Contact War. Shepard could agree or refuse to endorse Saracino for the parliamentary seat, and separately could agree or refuse to make a public statement of support for his candidacy. Refusing to endorse Saracino gave two Paragon points, while endorsing him gave two Renegade points; either way Saracino was grateful for Shepard's respect of the democratic process and returned to the protest.

The journal entry was marked complete upon receipt, its text reflecting Shepard's decision. News reports cut from Mass Effect 2, later restored in Legendary Edition, showed the Terra Firma Party gaining parliamentary support if Shepard had supported Saracino, or Saracino pleading guilty to tax evasion if not. The assignment was written by Chris L'Etoile.

Citadel: Mysterious Stranger was an assignment planned during development of Mass Effect 2 and cut before release; the information is drawn from cut content and is not canon. Set on the Citadel, it involved a romantic relationship between an asari dancer and a Terra Firma politician. In the Dark Star Lounge, Commander Shepard would have overheard an asari dancer called Nara Selephais, who had been on a date with a human man and wished to see him again but could not find him. Offering to help, Shepard would be given a few hints to track him across the Citadel and would learn that the man, Akio, was a politician or diplomat for the Terra Firma party. Akio would ask Shepard to keep his identity secret from Nara. Returning to her, Shepard would choose between lying to honor Akio's request or telling her the truth, either decision concluding the assignment.

- This assignment was written by Chris L'Etoile. - News reports cut from Mass Effect 2 show Saracino and the Terra Firma Party either gaining Parliamentary support if Shepard supported him, or pleading guilty to tax evasion if Shepard did not.\[1]. Shanxi was a Systems Alliance colony near the Shanxi-Theta mass relay, a jumping-off point for local traffic and best known for its role in the First Contact War of 2157, when it was the site of several battles between the Systems Alliance and the Turian Hierarchy. Prior to 2186 it was the only human colony ever occupied by an alien race.

After a turian patrol fleet wiped out an Alliance expedition passing through the Shanxi-Theta relay, one ship escaped back to Shanxi. The colony commander sent a retaliatory force that destroyed the turian ships, but the turians escalated, sending more vessels through the relay and capturing Shanxi, though the defenders got a message drone out to Arcturus Station first. Besieged from orbit, the Alliance garrison fought a guerrilla campaign; the turians dropped orbital debris to level city blocks and starve out marine fire teams, and the garrison, with troops starving and civilians dying, eventually surrendered. The occupying turians then faced their own logistical problems because their biology required all food to be imported. Believing they had defeated the bulk of humanity's navy, they were unprepared when the Second Fleet under Admiral Kastanie Drescher counterattacked and drove them off. The turians mobilized for full-scale war, but the Citadel Council, alarmed at Alliance capability, intervened and brokered a truce.

In Mass Effect: Evolution, a turian research vessel carrying an artifact crash-landed on Shanxi during the siege. General Desolas was sent to recover it; he was briefly captured by the human mercenaries Jack Harper, Ben Hislop and Eva Coré before the artifact incapacitated Harper and Hislop, letting the turians escape, recover the artifact and take the humans prisoner, who were later freed in a post-war exchange at Arcturus Station.

Shanxi bred lasting human-turian mistrust but also proved humanity's tenacity and military strength, impressing the galactic community since, apart from the krogan, the turians had found no equals in war. Xenophobic groups like Terra Firma cited Shanxi against alien contact; party leader Charles Saracino used it rhetorically, and a 2173 Terra Firma rally there was to be attended by candidate Claude Menneau, who vanished en route. Ashley Williams's grandfather, General Williams, was the commander who surrendered Shanxi, an act that ended his career though no charges were brought. During the Reaper War the Shanxi-Theta relay's traffic information was listed as "unavailable."

Humanity's first contact with an alien race occurred in 2157\. At that time, the Alliance allowed survey fleets to activate any dormant mass relays discovered, a practice considered dangerous and irresponsible by Council\-aligned races. When a turian patrol discovered a human fleet attempting to activate a relay, they attacked. One human vessel survived, retreating to the colony of Shanxi. The turians followed, quickly defeating the local forces. Shanxi was occupied, the first \-\- and, to date, only \-\- human world to be conquered by an alien species. The turians believed the handful of ships they defeated represented the bulk of human defenses, so they were unprepared when the Second Fleet under Admiral Kastanie Drescher launched a strong counteroffensive, evicting them from Shanxi. The turians mobilized for full\-scale war, drawing the attention of the rest of the galaxy. The Council quickly intervened, forcing a truce. Fortunately for humanity, the First Contact War was ended with a diplomatic solution.

Shanxi is sometimes used as an example by xenophobic political groups like Terra Firma to protest against humanity's growing interactions with alien races. In response to arguments that the turian actions at the Shanxi\-Theta relay were all a big misunderstanding, equivalent to snatching a gun away from a child, Terra Firma leader Charles Saracino responds that he would take the gun away from the child, "but I wouldn't shoot them dead." The First Contact War and the Battle of Shanxi created great mistrust between humans and turians. However, Shanxi also proved humanity's tenacity and military strength. It impressed the turians and the galactic community as a whole, because apart from the krogan, the turians had previously found no equals in war. The battle created a lot of interest in humans on the Citadel. |  | ***“This mission just got a lot more complicated.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

This page contains under ~150 words of real prose. Abrudas was a turian lieutenant who served in the First Contact War in 2157, under the command of General Desolas Arterius. Her soldiers found a downed turian research vessel that had crashed on Shanxi. Acting on a false message from Desolas, she led a squad to rendezvous with the General, fell into a trap, and unwittingly gave human mercenaries the location of the downed research vessel. She was the first female turian visually depicted in the Mass Effect franchise, and the events are detailed in Mass Effect: Evolution.

Commanded by Admiral Kastanie Drescher during the First Contact War of 2157, the Second Fleet was responsible for the liberation of Shanxi from turian occupation. Part of the Second Fleet was made up of materiel and volunteers from Elysium. During the Reaper invasion in 2186, the Second Fleet helps defend Arcturus Station. Admiral Hackett is eventually forced to sacrifice the entire fleet to give the Third and Fifth Fleets a chance to escape.

The First Contact War, called the Relay 314 Incident by the turians, was a three-month, low-intensity conflict between the human Systems Alliance and the Turian Hierarchy in 2157. After discovering the Charon Relay, humans expanded rapidly and activated every mass relay they could find. Turian patrols found human explorers reactivating the dormant Relay 314, an act forbidden under Citadel regulations imposed after the Rachni Wars. Rather than negotiate, the turians opened fire; one human ship escaped to warn the Alliance, and a retaliatory force destroyed the turian vessels, escalating the situation into war. To the turians it was a police action against a law-breaking species; to humanity it was first contact with alien life.

Humanity, its resources stretched thin by exploration, sent probes armed with nuclear fusion warheads into turian space to prevent technology capture, and lost several scout and patrol fleets. The soldier Tadius Ahern and a small squad held off dozens of turian soldiers for five minutes until evacuation. The turians broke through to Shanxi, humanity's nearest colony, and laid a protracted orbital siege that starved the defenders until General Williams, grandfather of Ashley Williams, surrendered the garrison. A month later Admiral Kastanie Drescher led the Second Fleet against Shanxi, surprising the turians and driving them off the planet. Both sides prepared for full-scale interplanetary war.

The Citadel Council intervened to negotiate peace, and humanity learned of the Citadel and the wider community of species. Only 623 human lives were lost, with slightly more turian casualties; the war's end became known as Armistice Day. The conflict gave humanity a galactic reputation as aggressors, fostered Alliance xenophobia, and contributed to the rise of pro-human groups such as Terra Firma and Cerberus. Some nuclear-armed probes remained at large as an Alliance secret. The turians were ordered to pay heavy reparations. Saren Arterius nurtured a lasting hatred of humanity after his brother's death. Relations later improved somewhat, exemplified by the joint human-turian construction of the SSV Normandy. If Shepard saved the Council during Sovereign's attack, the Hierarchy later considered additional reparations; if not, news reports described renewed distrust and turian military buildup.

General Williams was the Systems Alliance commander of the garrison on Shanxi when the First Contact War broke out in 2157. After humans were caught activating Relay 314, a turian patrol fleet destroyed an Alliance expeditionary fleet and broke through to Shanxi, the nearest human colony, beginning a siege with orbital bombardment. Cut off from reinforcements, Williams commanded a desperate guerrilla campaign from the surface, but turian tactics were overwhelming, with entire city blocks destroyed to eliminate small marine teams. Believing the only way to save Shanxi's population was surrender, Williams did so, becoming the only human commander to surrender to an alien force. Shanxi was soon liberated by the Alliance Second Fleet, and the Citadel Council brokered a truce before full-scale war.

Williams fell into disgrace, was brought to Earth in handcuffs, and though never formally charged, was demoted, assigned to desk jobs, and retired a year after Shanxi's liberation, spending his remaining days working construction in the colonies. His disgrace stained his family: his son never rose above serviceman third class, and his granddaughter Ashley Williams was kept from fleet postings and relegated to colony garrison duty. Alliance historians' attempts to exonerate him failed.

In Mass Effect: Evolution, Williams armed and trained a group of mercenaries, including Jack Harper, to fight the turians on Shanxi. Convinced the turians sought something on the planet beyond humans, he gave Harper's team a Mako and a captured turian prisoner before ordering a retreat to Arcturus Station. He drank on the job under the stress. Weeks later he presided over a prisoner exchange at Arcturus, where Harper's prisoner proved to be turian General Desolas Arterius, who had captured Harper and Eva Coré; when Desolas tried to take Harper back, Williams ordered him off Arcturus. Williams offered condolences over the death of Harper's teammate Ben Hislop, disagreed with the Alliance's new policy of peaceful coexistence, planned to resign his command, and gave his awarded personal shuttle to Harper and Coré to aid their investigation. His story is told during Ashley's conversations with Commander Shepard.

Lieutenant James Vega was a human Systems Alliance Marine and a member of Commander Shepard's squad in 2186. An experienced soldier but unfamiliar with galactic politics and the criminal underworld, he was written primarily by Mac Walters and intended to reflect a new player's perspective. He was originally named James Sanders before the name was changed.

Per Mass Effect: Homeworlds, Vega joined the Marines at Camp Pendleton in 2176 with the encouragement of his uncle Emilio Vega, despite his father Joshua "Josh" Sanders trying to trap him into a life as an errand boy through a coerced drug run in San Diego. Emilio convinced James that only he could choose how to live.

In Mass Effect: Paragon Lost, Vega served as second-in-command of Delta Squad on the colony Fehl Prime under Captain Toni. After defeating a Blood Pack siege in single combat with the krogan Archuk, Delta Squad was assigned as colony security. Two years later the Collectors attacked; with Toni incapacitated, Vega took command. His decision to fire the colony defense cannons at half power failed, alerting the Collector ship. Betrayed by the undercover Cerberus/Collector agent Messner, and unable to save both the asari anthropologist Treeya (who carried vital intel) and the colonists, Vega chose to save Treeya and the intel, sacrificing the colony. He was commended and promoted but felt he was no hero. He later learned Shepard had destroyed the Collectors without the intel, meaning the colony died for nothing. This guilt drove him to reckless behavior. In Mass Effect: Conviction, Anderson recruited him from Omega to guard the Alliance brig holding the surrendered Shepard.

In Mass Effect 3, Vega escorted Shepard to the defense committee hearing interrupted by the Reaper attack on Earth, then helped extract Shepard aboard the Normandy. On Mars he crashed his shuttle into Dr. Eva Coré's to stop her escaping with the Prothean data. He served as squadmate throughout the war, based in the Shuttle Bay bantering with his friend Steve Cortez, doing pull-ups, and sparring with Shepard, to whom he confided the Fehl Prime story. He nicknamed people ("Loco" for male Shepard, "Lola" for female, "Scars" for Garrus, "Sparks" for Tali, "Esteban" for Cortez). He noted his father's surname was Sanders but that he was unrelated to Kahlee Sanders. Offered N7 training and doubtful he deserved it, he ultimately accepted, celebrating with a back tattoo. A female Shepard with no prior commitments could romance him. If Shepard could not rally enough forces, Vega could be killed by Harbinger during the final push to the conduit; otherwise he survived and honored Shepard at the Memorial Wall. He was voiced by Freddie Prinze, Jr.

*For his gameplay attributes, see Squad Members Guide (Mass Effect 3\)\#James Vega.* James Vega is tasked to escort Shepard to an Alliance defense committee hearing, but the hearing is interrupted when the Reapers attack Earth. Vega and Ashley Williams/Kaidan Alenko (depending on who survived Virmire) retrieve the Normandy SR\-2 and extract Shepard. Voluntarily staying behind to help organize a resistance, Anderson convinces Shepard to leave Earth to seek help from the Citadel Council. Vega is displeased on hearing this and wants to stay behind as well; Shepard overrules him with the stark military logic of the plan, upsetting Vega who nonetheless lets the matter drop for now. During a mission to the Prothean archives on Mars, after Shepard and Ashley/Kaidan reunite with Liara, Shepard sends Vega outside the research facility to safeguard the team's exit. While this order again frustrates James, it proves very fortuitous. Dr. Eva Coré, revealed to be a Cerberus mole, almost escapes Mars in possession of the only remaining copy of translated Prothean data that may contain the secret to defeating the Reapers, but a waiting Vega crashes his own shuttle into hers, narrowly averting disaster. Eva, further revealed to be a synthetic in the crash, is disabled by Shepard, and the Commander orders the squad to her back with them. Vega complies, slinging the seemingly lifeless android over his shoulder and dumping it in the medbay outside the AI Core. Later on the Citadel, Shepard may speak with Vega again on the Presidium under relaxed circumstances for the first time since Vancouver. Vega comments on the quiet, noting how peaceful the Citadel is, pointing out its only a facade because the people living there are isolated from the Reaper threat and are in denial. Vega finally admits that leaving Earth was the correct decision for Shepard to make; the other races needed the wake\-up call, and humanity can't stop the Reapers without their help. As the Commander is leaving, James says he's heading down to the parts of the Citadel where they "keep it real" if Shepard wants to meet him there sometime. Vega normally loiters in the Shuttle Bay by a weapons bench, occasionally bantering with his good friend Steve Cortez over topics of interest. The first time Shepard visits Vega in the Shuttle Bay, James is doing some pull\-ups using the overhead bars in his turf. Depending on how far along Shepard is on the track to saving the galaxy, Vega's reactions run the whole gamut. Immediately after Shepard debriefs the Council about the Crucible, getting the usual noncommittal and unhelpful responses and being informed they have to rescue a turian primarch from Palaven, James reveals he's never been to the turian homeworld. If he was doing pull\-ups by the time Garrus is welcomed aboard, he says he'll take Shepard's word about the turian for it as he can't tell turians apart. If EDI's got herself a shiny robot body, Vega asks instead if Shepard was "shitting" him, and his Commander replies "I shit you not." If Shepard is male, James poses the question if he's just there to inform him about EDI. If Shepard delays talking to him for much farther, James wonders instead what the Commander is doing below decks with the "grunts", voicing aloud he was starting to think Shepard doesn't like him. If Shepard really delayed in talking to him, the first thing Vega asks the Commander is if they "took a wrong turn at the elevator", by now firmly thinking Shepard didn't know or cared to know where to find him. Whatever the circumstances of their first meet, they eventually get into a sparring match, where James gives a brief summary of his activities before joining the Normandy. If Shepard really refrained from talking to him James promises to go easy, "just in case." James narrates that his old CO, Captain Toni, a "hard\-assed son of a bitch" but a "good leader" in Vega's words, was killed along with most of Vega's squad while the squad was protecting a civilian colony from a Collector attack. The leadership vacuum caused by Captain Toni falling in battle was filled in by Vega himself, and he had to make a choice between saving the colony or saving the intel the squad had recovered that could be used to destroy the Collectors. Vega chose to save the intel, but found out far too late that his choice was rendered completely unnecessary since Shepard managed to destroy the Collector threat without the intel Vega saved, which meant that Vega allowed the colony to die for nothing.

Milque was a human sniper and member of Delta Squad, an Alliance special-forces unit deployed to the colony of Fehl Prime, as depicted in the animated film Mass Effect: Paragon Lost. A cautious, cynical man with a dry sense of humor, he was often taken for a coward but obeyed orders and reliably covered his teammates, usually in exchange for free drinks. Armed with an M-92 Mantis, he was the squad's marksman.

Delta Squad first arrived on Fehl Prime around 2183 to repel a Blood Pack mercenary attack. Milque's unit was shot down during a strafing run from a Kodiak shuttle; Lieutenant James Vega took command after Captain Toni was incapacitated. Milque surrendered his power cells to Vega, covered his charge against the krogan Battlemaster Archuk, was grazed across the collarbone by the mercenary Brood, and recovered in time to kill Archuk and save Vega. The Blood Pack were defeated and Milque was commended.

Two years later, with Fehl Prime rebuilt and fortified with an anti-ship cannon, Delta Squad investigated a jamming signal and found an alien artifact, which Vega ordered destroyed. The colony was then attacked by the Collectors, who harvested colonists aboard a ship. The squad's counterattacks failed; the defense cannon could not penetrate the ship's barriers, and a Praetorian containing Kamille's torso killed Mason. The survivors escaped in the imprisoned Brood's ship in exchange for freeing him. Vega spiked the group's drink flask with a cure for the seeker plague. Brood was shot dead by the Cerberus informant Messner while attacking the Collector ship, and the group was captured. Milque, Essex and Vega synthesized more antidote through the Collectors' systems and revived the colonists. Milque, who had washed out of pilot training, was made to fly a captured freighter, using it to rescue Vega at the ship's core. Forced to choose, Vega saved Treeya and her intel rather than the colonists, and the Collector ship crashed with everyone aboard killed; Milque judged it the wrong choice. Vega was later commended, promoted and invited into the N7 program. Milque joined Vega and Treeya at the Fehl Prime Memorial Monument to honor the dead.

However, Kamille is abducted by the Collectors in the chaos. Outside the bunker's entrance, Vega and Essex hold off hordes of enemies while Nicky hacks through the bunker security. Mason and Milque then arrive in the nick of time and seal off the Collectors' approach by causing a cave\-in. Mason is furious at Essex for failing to watch Kamille's back. Vega chastises them for quarreling and shouts at them to fall back. The squad retreats into the bunker with Essex covering them with his biotics. Once inside, Vega formulates a new plan: to escape in the freighter Messner arrived in. However, the plan doesn't last long as the Collector vessel incinerates the ship as if it has heard Vega's plan. Messner then brings up Vega's unintended wrong choice, which causes Mason to vent his fury at him. Vega unflinchingly says that he hasn't given up on anyone yet and stresses the necessity of fighting together and setting aside differences. He and Nicky then proceed to bring Essex's paralyzed form inside the bunker. Vega orders Nicky to use the Alliance databases to find a possible cure for the paralysis. While searching, Nicky comes up with a startling find: Messner is an undercover Cerberus agent. Vega is furious at this revelation, hitting Messner across the face while explaining to Treeya about Cerberus goals. He relents once Messner asserts Cerberus is looking for a cure to the seeker swarm paralysis too. A new distraction occurs when Brood, who is being kept as a test subject in the labs, struggles to free himself from confinement. Vega quickly goes to meet Brood and despite Brood's promises to help them escape the colony, decides not to trust him. Later, being by himself while Nicky continues the search for a cure, Vega reflects on his past decisions. Noticing how he is awfully quiet, Treeya comes to console Vega. Vega quietly asks if he made the right decision to fire the defense cannons at half power. Treeya honestly answers that he made what he thought was the best choice. When Vega talks about how Shepard would have made the right choice, Treeya firmly tells him Vega is not Shepard and that he should stop trying to act like him/her. She then bonds briefly with Vega who experiences a moment of peace. Nicky finally finds a cure which however fails to show any immediate effect on Essex. A Praetorian suddenly attacks the lab and tears through it, claiming the life of Mason, who impulsively approaches it on seeing Kamille's twisted form inside the creature's head. Vega and Milque open heavy fire on the Praetorian, but are unable to penetrate the heavy armor. While falling back, Vega decides to take a quick detour and frees Brood after forming an uneasy alliance. Brood leads the way to a hidden shuttle of his and the team board it and tries to get away as fast as it can. The Praetorian follows however and despite the sustained fire from Vega, Milque and Nicky, it manages to stab the latter in the gut when he steps in to take the blow meant for Vega, wounding him mortally. Vega, aghast and furious at the casualty, jumps onto the Praetorian's back which is now held in a stasis by a revived Essex. Vega discharges his gun into the Praetorian's skull at point\-blank range and the enemy is defeated at last, falling into the industrial vats. After being hauled back into the ship by Essex, Vega immediately goes to a dying Nicky and tries to apply first\-aid but his efforts are in vain as the marine breathes his last after urging Vega to save the colonists. Hidden for the moment, the squad sets the shuttle down in a safe spot and commences repairs. Vega decides to take the fight to the Collectors by infiltrating their ship. Quietly, he slips the seeker swarm antidote into his flask containing a drink and offers it to everyone, encouraging them to use Brood's idea of punching straight through the Collector weapons port. The plan is then to disable the ship's drive core and save the colonists. The shuttle then goes airborne and punches through the desired spot flawlessly. Vega, Essex and Milque then proceed to defend the shuttle from incoming Collector troopers, using Brood's store of heavy weapons. Even Treeya joins the fight and Vega compliments her, causing her to blush. Messner shows his true colors at this time and shoots Brood in the head as he is about to take out the drive core, causing the shuttle to make a crash landing. Vega, Essex and Milque are captured and paralyzed by the Collectors while Treeya is forced away by Messner, who is actually working for the Collectors.

Priority: Mars was the first full mission of Mass Effect 3, acquired automatically after the Reaper assault on Earth in the prologue. Admiral Hackett ordered the Normandy to the Prothean archives on Mars, where the dig site had gone silent, to recover data that might help defeat the Reapers. Shepard landed with James Vega and found Cerberus troops executing Alliance researchers; this was the first appearance of Cerberus as an enemy faction in the trilogy, introducing Assault Troopers, Centurions and Guardians. Among the dead was a researcher named Reeves.

Inside the facility Shepard reunited with Dr. Liara T'Soni, who revealed she had discovered Prothean plans for a device ("the Crucible") capable of stopping the Reapers, and that Cerberus was there to seize them. Shepard sent Vega back to the shuttle to protect the team's exit and took Liara as squadmate. The two fought through the research complex, a sabotaged cafeteria where the air had been vented, corridors, a clean room, an autoturret gauntlet and a tram station, learning that Cerberus operatives had been implanted with Reaper technology. Shepard posed as a Cerberus team to lure a tram, then fought through a large battle at the archive station.

In the archive chamber the Illusive Man appeared by hologram. The Cerberus infiltrator Dr. Eva Coré was caught stealing the Prothean data, triggering a rooftop chase. Eva reached a shuttle, but Vega crashed his shuttle into hers. Her organic disguise was destroyed, revealing a mech infiltration unit, and on the Illusive Man's order she gravely injured Kaidan Alenko or Ashley Williams before Shepard shot her down. Shepard ordered the body brought aboard the Normandy, which left Mars orbit just as the Reapers arrived. The wounded crewmate was taken to the medical bay, and Shepard ordered Joker to set course for the Citadel. Hackett confirmed Anderson's order to seek Council aid and requested the Crucible plans for Alliance analysis. Eva's body would later be reactivated by EDI.

Shepard can invite Vega and Cortez for a night of drinks and watching biotiball featuring the Seattle Sorcerers taking on the Usaru Maestros, before or after the party. Cortez sends an e\-mail asking for an invitation, if Shepard has helped him reach a sense of closure on his husband's death. Both Cortez and Vega state their cases for each team to win. Vega backs the Maestros and is teased by Cortez for it, who cites Vega's support of the Maestros is mostly due to their players being beautiful asari, than their actual skill. Vega sheepishly admits he has got the "hots" for the Maestro players. Shepard is asked to back a team. Selecting a particular team will result in the supporter of that team winning the bet (though the Sorcerers always win the game). Vega is disappointed when his team doesn't win and grudgingly admits defeat. When Shepard questions the nature of the bet, the winner reveals that the bet was only on whether the Commander would be correct in their pick, rather than who would actually win. After the game, both of them thank Shepard and leave the apartment. Vega is a mandatory invite to Shepard's big party. During the party a female Shepard with no prior commitments can support a hook\-up between herself and James. If this happens Shepard will wake up the next morning with James; however, he asks Shepard to not mention what happened to anyone else. In the first stages of the party Vega hangs out with Cortez on the couches in the living room. If Shepard sets a quiet party, James hangs out with Liara by the bar at the poker den, engaging in a debate over which ship is better: the SSV Normandy or the Normandy SR\-2. James favors the latter. At the conclusion of a quiet party, Vega plays poker with Liara in the den. If the party is set to energetic, James spends time at the apartment balcony with Liara and some of the other biotics in the party, namely Liara, Jacob, Jack, Miranda, and Kaidan/Ashley, if they're present. Vega claims physical training trumps biotics, much to the incredulity of the others. Liara challenges this claim and both of them exchange friendly barbs, with the others supporting Liara. Vega then proceeds to show off his "fine example of peak physical form". Ashley, if present, shows interest beyond professionalism in Vega, to which he reacts favorably. If Shepard favors physical training, James shows satisfaction at her choice and then points out that he can roll his tongue as well. Later, Liara tells James she's going to challenge him to a pull\-up contest, something which causes James to give pause, unsure if he should accept the challenge. If Shepard favors biotics, Vega reluctantly accepts the decision. In the next stage of the party, James demonstrates the result of the debate. If Shepard sided with biotics, Liara gives James a demonstration of her powers by biotically lifting him with seemingly no effort. Vega comments on feeling "fuzzy" all over, "among other things." If Shepard chose physical training instead, Vega (plus Jacob and/or Kaidan if they're present) do push\-ups. If Kasumi is also around, she sits on top of Vega while cloaked. Vega naturally finds it difficult to keep up with Jacob, much to his consternation. Kasumi finally reveals herself when Vega is tired out and the marine collapses at that instant. When the party gets lively, Vega may flirt with Ashley if she is present. Shepard can either encourage the exchange or tell them to cool it. If encouraged, Vega continues his playful banter, attempting to woo her with the Spanish phrase *"tú con tantas curvas, y yo sin frenos"* (“you with such curves, and me with no brakes”). Ashley, amused, keeps asking him to repeat it until Vega becomes confused—ultimately resulting in nothing more than lighthearted, harmless flirting. If they don't continue flirting, James instead dances with the other balcony guests. He favors a fist\-pumping moveset akin to aerobic exercise. In the morning after the party, he cooks eggs for the guests, encouraging them all to try his eggs.

Days after the destruction of Bahak, the galaxy is in turmoil over Commander Shepard's alleged actions. While the Citadel Council denounces the Commander and Councilor Udina deflects blame from the Systems Alliance, the Batarian Hegemony calls for retribution for the apparent terrorist acts. On Omega, Alliance soldier James Vega plays cards in a bar as he watches a newscast about the uproar. Without warning, he rips the screen from the wall, offering to pay the krogan bartender for the damages. The batarians Vega was playing cards with become confrontational and accuse him of being a "Shepard Lover". Vega tries to calm them down, but they charge him. He bashes one batarian over the head with the screen, then rushes the leader of another group, both of them crashing through a window. The rest of the batarians surround Vega and attack. The fight is interrupted by the arrival of Admiral Anderson and a contingent of soldiers. Anderson informs Vega that he is being brought in for more training. As they board an aircar, Anderson tells Vega that he must get past "the incident on Fehl" and "be the soldier \[they] expect of \[him]". Vega argues, demanding that Anderson throw him in the brig as they approach the Normandy SR\-2. Anderson then explains that Vega will actually be guarding the brig, and one special prisoner: Commander Shepard.

evidence.text:
Mason was a member of Delta Squad, an Alliance special forces unit deployed to Fehl Prime in 2185. He was a shuttle pilot, talented but always talking about quitting, and a brave, tenacious marine in a relationship with squadmate Kamille. Delta Squad was deployed to stop a Blood Pack mercenary invasion of Fehl Prime. Mason skillfully piloted a Kodiak drop shuttle and pounded Blood Pack positions from the air until a missile hit forced a crash landing. Shaken but undeterred, he joined the initial Alliance counterattack in light armor, took a shoulder hit, and lay low for the rest of the firefight; acting CO James Vega nicknamed him "flyboy" and ordered him to tend the incapacitated Captain Toni. The battle went to the marines thanks to Vega's tactics, and Mason said Vega deserved "a goddamn medal."

Two years later, Fehl Prime was flourishing and installing new defenses due to Terminus colony disappearances. Mason was puzzled by the buildup and teased Vega about his attraction to the asari anthropologist Treeya. Captain Toni ordered Delta Squad to investigate a jamming signal from an artifact on the colony's outskirts; with the APC down, Mason drove the squad there in a second-hand M35 Mako from Messner. He stayed with the Mako as cover while the squad investigated, and was present when the artifact was destroyed by Essex and Treeya contacted Liara T'Soni about it. A Collector ship then arrived and began harvesting the population.

The squad planned to use the colony defense cannons against the vessel. Mason sabotaged the fuel depots as a distraction, then saved Milque from a Collector trooper. Vega, on Treeya's suggestion, fired the cannon at half power; the underpowered shot was deflected and nearly killed the team. Mason and Milque fought through Collectors aboard a colony tram to rejoin the others, and Mason caused a cave-in to seal a passage. He learned of Kamille's loss from Essex, her partner at the time, and blamed both Essex and later Vega for the half-power decision before grudgingly calming down. He accompanied Vega and Milque to investigate the lab's lower levels, finding the Blood Pack krogan Brood caged and used as a test subject, whom the squad left. When a Praetorian breached the lab's door, Kamille's head was visible among the skulls in its head; Mason walked toward the creature seeing only Kamille and was incinerated by its particle beam.

evidence.text: The Systems Alliance dispatches a team of soldiers to Fehl Prime in 2183 in response to Blood Pack mercenaries laying siege to the colony. Most of the troops are killed, but thanks to the leadership qualities of Lieutenant James Vega the survivors manage to turn the tide and proceed to wipe out the mercs. Anderson and Admiral Hackett commend the Lieutenant for his actions, ordering his squad to stay put in the colony for its continued safety because of its importance. Two years later, Alliance Command provides military\-grade kinetic barriers and a defense cannon for the colony's protection. This is due to a spate of human colony disappearances in the Terminus Systems, where Fehl Prime is located. The official word they give to their subordinates when asked, however, is "no comment". Most people on Fehl Prime are happy with the Alliance help, with a few exceptions because their work is repeatedly being interfered with. Soon enough, a massive Collector vessel arrives on the colony and begins harvesting the human population. The kinetic barriers prove useless against the deployed Seeker Swarms and the defense cannon ultimately gets destroyed, having been fired at the alien ship at half power out of concern for civilian casualties. Nevertheless, the surviving Alliance soldiers manage to obtain some good from the fiasco, salvaging intel about the invaders, dubbed Collectors, but at the cost of the colony itself. Anderson and Admiral Hackett promote Vega for this and bestow him an N7 commendation. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.text:
Nicky was a member of Delta Squad, an Alliance special forces unit deployed to the colony of Fehl Prime in 2185, as depicted in the animated film Mass Effect: Paragon Lost. He served as the team's technical specialist and was highly talented at his job, though shy and timid. He respected the chain of command and showed great deference to Lieutenant James Vega, persistently calling him "sir" despite Vega's objections.

Delta Squad was sent to Fehl Prime to stop a Blood Pack invasion. Worried by the last-minute orders, Nicky analyzed the mission thoroughly. The Kodiak shuttle was shot down during descent. In the counter-assault Nicky provided tactical readouts of enemy positions and deployed his Combat Drone, which distracted the Blood Pack leader Archuk long enough to buy Vega time. Nicky was then wounded by a sniper shot from Brood and was incapacitated for the rest of the firefight. He was commended afterward.

Two years later, with Fehl Prime flourishing but new defense cannons installed amid a spate of Terminus colony disappearances, Nicky suspected the guns were connected to those disappearances. Captain Toni ordered Delta Squad to investigate a jamming signal emitted by an alien artifact in nearby Prothean ruins; the artifact was destroyed by Essex after Nicky failed to interface with it. When a Collector ship arrived, Nicky could not contact the colony. The squad tried to use the colony defense cannons against the vessel, but Vega, impatient with the slow charge, ordered a half-power shot that was deflected and nearly killed the team. Retreating into a bunker, Nicky's database search for an antidote to seeker-swarm toxin instead flagged squad member Messner as a Cerberus operative, forcing an uneasy alliance. After a Praetorian attack drove the squad onto Brood's ship, the creature attacked the shuttle in flight; Nicky was mortally wounded by its leg while pushing Vega clear of a melee attack. As he died, he urged Vega to save the colonists.

evidence.text:
Messner was a trader who arrived on Fehl Prime in 2185, presenting himself as a traveling merchant selling hardware around the galaxy. In truth he was a Cerberus operative tasked with investigating the disappearances of human colonies and the Collectors' involvement, as depicted in Mass Effect: Paragon Lost.

Delivering a shipment to Fehl Prime, Messner met James Vega and Treeya en route to the colony's underground research labs, flattering Vega for his 2183 victory. Barred from the newly secured labs, he lent Delta Squad a M35 Mako to investigate a jamming signal on the colony outskirts. While the squad destroyed the alien bio-mechanical device producing the signal, a Collector ship arrived and began harvesting the population; Messner suggested using the colony defense cannons against it, but a low-powered shot failed to disable the ship. In the labs Delta Squad learned the tightened security had been meant to keep Messner out, the Alliance having identified him as a Cerberus agent. He admitted it, arguing they now shared the goal of stopping the Collectors.

When Delta Squad used a ship piloted by the krogan Brood to attack the Collector ship's drive core, Messner shot Brood in the head, causing the ship to crash and the squad to be captured. He revealed he had deliberately lured the Collectors to Fehl Prime with the jamming device to study them, sacrificing the colony to gain their temporary trust. He forced Treeya, who could interface with Prothean technology, to access a Prothean archive aboard the ship, revealing the Protheans' last stand, their transformation into Collectors, and a plan to liquefy humans into genetic material for a new Reaper. Messner recorded the intel on a bracelet for Cerberus. The Collectors then declared him no longer useful and prepared a pod for his "ascension"; he threw Treeya into it instead, but she seized the bracelet as the pod was ejected toward Fehl Prime. In the ensuing firefight Vega disarmed and stabbed Messner, refused his bribes, and left him to be killed by Collector fire.

evidence.text: In 2183, the human colony of Fehl Prime, a major producer of pharmaceuticals for the Systems Alliance, comes under attack by a group of Blood Pack mercenaries led by the krogan Archuk. In response, the Alliance dispatches several teams of Marines to aid the beleaguered colonists. During the landing attempt, each of the Alliance shuttles are shot down by the Blood Pack. Only one Marine unit, Delta Squad, survives the crash landing of their shuttle, but the Blood Pack execute several members before the rest can retreat to cover. Lieutenant James Vega stays behind to help Delta Squad's commanding officer, Captain Toni, whose leg was badly broken in the crash. Vega sets Toni's leg, causing him to scream and alert the Blood Pack to their presence. Under heavy fire, Vega and Toni scramble to meet up with the rest of the squad, consisting of Kamille, Nicky, Milque, Essex, and Mason. When Archuk challenges Delta Squad to show themselves and fight, Vega decides to duel Archuk, distracting the Blood Pack while Kamille and Essex flank them and ambush from behind. Nicky aids Vega by sending out a combat drone, while Milque provides covering fire with his sniper rifle. At first, Vega is outmatched by Archuk, unable to penetrate the krogan's heavy shields, but with the help of Nicky's drone, Archuk's shields are overloaded and Vega is able to chip away at his armor. Archuk charges and grabs Vega, but Milque kills the krogan before Archuk can strike the final blow. Meanwhile, Kamille and Essex take out the remaining Blood Pack. The sole survivor, Archuk's second\-in\-command Brood, is spared by Vega and taken prisoner. In the aftermath, Admiral Steven Hackett orders Delta Squad to remain on Fehl Prime and protect it from future attacks.

evidence.page: Anderson Stays Behind as the Normandy Leaves Earth
evidence.text: Anderson Stays Behind as the Normandy Leaves Earth. 2186, Vancouver, Earth, the first hours of the Reaper invasion (Prologue: Earth) a Systems Alliance HQ tower in Vancouver, then the ruined streets and spaceport, then the Normandy SR-2 shuttle bay Six months after Bahak, Shepard was under arrest and relieved of command in Vancouver. Anderson escorted the Commander, with Lieutenant James Vega, into a Systems Alliance defense committee meeting, where Shepard confirmed the committee's fear that the Reapers had returned and were coming for Earth. Contact was lost with Luna Base mid-meeting; a Reaper capital ship then descended over the city and blasted the tower, killing the committee and staff. Only Shepard and Anderson walked out.

They raised the Virmire survivor — Ashley Williams or Kaidan Alenko — by radio and told them to get to the Normandy. evidence.page: Anderson Stays Behind as the Normandy Leaves Earth
evidence.text: Anderson Stays Behind as the Normandy Leaves Earth. 2186, Vancouver, Earth, the first hours of the Reaper invasion (Prologue: Earth) a Systems Alliance HQ tower in Vancouver, then the ruined streets and spaceport, then the Normandy SR-2 shuttle bay As Shepard moved to board, Anderson refused to leave — a million more survivors like the men behind them needed a leader — and stayed on Earth to raise a resistance. He threw Shepard the dog tags that reinstated the Commander in the Alliance and charged Shepard with bringing back help from the Council. Shepard protested; Anderson did not change his mind.

Six months have passed since the destruction of Bahak and Commander Shepard's voluntary return to the Alliance. The Commander has been relieved of command and detained in a Systems Alliance facility in the city of Vancouver on Earth. Without warning, Alliance deep space outposts beyond Sol begin to go dark. Admiral Steven Hackett, the head of the Alliance military, begins to prepare for an imminent invasion. Admiral David Anderson arrives in Vancouver and escorts Commander Shepard with Lieutenant James Vega to a meeting with an Alliance defense committee. Shepard confirms their worst fears: the Reapers have returned to the galaxy and are on their way to Earth. At that moment, contact is lost with Luna Base and news reports begin to surface of an unknown alien force landing in Earth's cities. The Reapers have already arrived. A Reaper capital ship then descends through the clouds over Vancouver and blasts the Alliance building, killing the defense committee and Alliance staff. Shepard and Anderson survive and contact Ashley Williams or Kaidan Alenko (whichever survived Virmire), telling them to get to the Normandy. As Shepard and Anderson make their way from building to building to get to the spaceport, Anderson tells Shepard that they have to get to the Citadel and seek help from the Council. They reach a comm set near a crashed gunship and hail the Normandy to evacuate. After holding off an attack from Cannibals, the Normandy bombs the area clear of attackers. As Shepard boards the ship, Anderson informs the Commander that he will stay behind to lead the resistance, and hands over Shepard's dog tags. Shepard protests, but Anderson charges Shepard with getting as much help as possible to save Earth and stop the Reapers. As the Normandy lifts off, Shepard witnesses a child running to an Alliance evacuation area and boarding a shuttle. As the shuttles lift off, a Reaper destroyer emerges from behind a cluster of buildings and targets the shuttles, killing those who were aboard including the child. Distraught, Shepard steps away from the open shuttle bay doors of the Normandy, and the ship escapes Earth as more Reapers and the wreckage of Alliance ships rain down upon the planet.

Prologue: Earth is the opening mission of Mass Effect 3, acquired automatically at the start of the game. It serves as the game's tutorial. After character customization and a series of cutscenes with morality-point dialogue, Shepard enters a training stage in war-torn Vancouver during the Reaper invasion. Anderson gives Shepard an M-3 Predator pistol, and the two move across rooftops while Oculi destroy Alliance fighters overhead. Shepard encounters husks climbing a wall and a child fleeing toward a building; Anderson eventually runs out of ammo and climbs down a ladder. Shepard fights husks in melee before a Reaper fires its laser at an adjacent building.

Moving through the ruins, Shepard opens a med kit, briefly encounters the boy again, and then witnesses an Alliance vessel destroyed by a Reaper while Ashley Williams or Kaidan Alenko comments over the radio. Shepard reaches two Alliance soldiers and fights the first engagement against Cannibals, which here do not use grenades. Anderson can now deal damage and be assigned squad points. After crossing a bridge, salvaging a second med kit, and picking up an M-8 Avenger, Shepard activates a radio and fights further Cannibal waves until the Normandy SR-2 arrives and clears the remaining enemies.

Shepard says goodbye to Anderson, who stays on Earth. The boy is killed when the Kodiak evacuating him is shot down by a Destroyer. The Normandy leaves Vancouver, passing burning human fleets. Aboard ship, James Vega is incredulous that Shepard intends to follow Anderson's orders and leave Earth to seek the Citadel Council's aid; the exchange allows Paragon or Renegade interrupts. Admiral Hackett then contacts Shepard and assigns the next mission, Priority: Mars.

Enemies are Cannibals and Husks. Rewards include three units of medi-gel, the M-3 Predator, and the M-8 Avenger. Trivia notes Vancouver was chosen because BioWare is a Canadian company; the ship shown destroyed is actually an Alliance cruiser rather than the dreadnought Ashley or Kaidan describe, a discrepancy noted in SolComms reports by Emily Wong; and fleeing civilians visible in the distance are 2D sprites resembling Jack.
**Firebase Vancouver** is a multiplayer map included in Mass Effect 3: Earth. It is set in Vancouver.

- After kicking around several cities about where Mass Effect 3 should open, Vancouver was eventually chosen because it is a Canadian city, BioWare is a Canadian company and it had just finished the 2010 Winter Olympics. The style of the city was designed to reflect hope and included several major known Vancouver Landmarks. - There is cut dialogue where Shepard agrees with Anderson's advice to get to the Citadel and talk to the Council. - During the mission, Ashley Williams or Kaidan Alenko can be heard over the radio commenting on the imminent destruction of an Alliance dreadnought as it confronts a Reaper. The ship's destruction is witnessed by the player, but the model of ship shown is actually an Alliance cruiser. According to BioWare, by the time the mistake was realized, it was too late to re\-record Ashley and Kaidan's dialogue or replace the ship in the scene. - The discrepancy is noted in the SolComms reports, in which Emily Wong is confused at the report, since dreadnoughts cannot enter the atmosphere. - At certain locations, it's possible to see civilians fleeing the invasion in the distance. Using external tools or Photo Mode in Legendary Edition allows for closer examination, revealing them to be 2D sprites of who appears to be Jack.
