Multiplayer map page. Firebase Vancouver is a Mass Effect 3 multiplayer map included in the Mass Effect 3: Earth DLC, set on rooftops in Vancouver. Its areas are the Helipad (starting location and a possible extraction zone), Lower Rooftops, Upper Rooftops (lower level a possible extraction zone), Offices (a medical wing), Ventilation Deck, and Ventilation Housing. Like Firebase Dagger, it has two possible extraction locations, close together. The Ventilation Deck is difficult to navigate for classes that cannot climb cover, and area-of-effect powers can singlehandedly halt massed infantry at chokepoints such as the ladder by the Offices.

Citadel: Old Friends was a Mass Effect assignment available only to a Commander Shepard with the Earthborn background, after one of the core missions had been completed: finding Liara T'Soni, Noveria: Matriarch Benezia, or Feros: The Thorian. Outside Chora's Den in the Wards, a human named Finch addressed Shepard in passing. Finch was a member of the Tenth Street Reds, a gang on Earth to which Shepard had once belonged, and said another member, Curt Weisman, had been arrested by the turians for a "minor offence" committed while in turian space. Finch wanted Shepard to talk to the turian guard in Chora's Den to secure Weisman's release, and threatened to reveal Shepard's shady past with the Reds otherwise.

From the guard, Shepard learned that the Reds had become a violent anti-alien group and that Weisman had been responsible for a hate crime, poisoning medical cargo meant for a turian colony that could have killed millions. Shepard could negotiate Weisman's release, inform the guard that Finch was likely to try to free the prisoner, or change course after hearing about the crime. Tipping the guard off gave Paragon points, while using Intimidate or Charm to free the prisoner gave Renegade points.

If Shepard did not free Weisman, Finch appeared and declared he would tell the galaxy that Shepard had once been affiliated with the Reds and their anti-alien agenda. Shepard could talk him down or simply shoot him; killing Finch impressed the turian guard, whereas letting him go made the guard think less of the first human Spectre. In Mass Effect 2, Shepard received a message from Finch titled "Hello from the Reds" encouraging Shepard's fight against the Collectors. The assignment was written by Trick Weekes and was named "Memories of Green" in the game's internal data.

District Guards were turians hired by Aria T'Loak to guard the quarantine zone on Omega during the plague outbreak in Mass Effect 2. After Shepard spoke with Aria about Mordin Solus and headed to the quarantine zone, the squad was confronted by a district guard at the transport hub. If Shepard convinced the guard to let them through, he radioed ahead for his companions to stand down; if Shepard failed, the guards opened fire on the squad's arrival.

The guards were armed with M-8 Avenger assault rifles. They had only health on lower difficulties and minor shielding on Hardcore and Insanity, and no biotic or tech powers. They compensated with disciplined use of cover and superior positioning, popping out to fire and ducking back down.

Shepard provides the couch; they bring the refreshments.

After Shepard's escape from the first run\-in with CAT6, Cortez loiters in the study room of the apartment. He's relieved the Commander got out as none of them expected the attack, so he shares an illuminating lesson learned from the event: "Never have dinner with Joker." If Shepard and Steve are lovers, he admonishes Shepard with another one: "You sneak off to a dinner date with another man, you get shot at." Cortez provides assistance during the infiltration into the Spectre Archives as part of Team Hammerhead, and provides suppressive fire with an M\-8 Avenger alongside the rest of the crew. While Shepard and company fight the Clone to retake the Normandy, Cortez and Joker fly a skycar directly ahead of the Normandy's trajectory, preventing the merc pilot from making the jump to FTL. Cortez utilises the full extent of his piloting skills to evade the Normandy's weapons fire. Once the clone is defeated, Cortez brings a restrained Maya Brooks to Shepard. When Joker compliments his "crazy stunt flying" in the shuttle, Cortez says it was nice to fly something more responsive than the Kodiak; if Cortez and Shepard are romantically involved, he'll instead respond that he was "motivated", followed by a sly wink at the Commander. After taking back the Normandy from the Clone, Cortez will send Shepard an invitation to the Silversun Strip. Steve picks Shepard up at the appointed location with the Kodiak to go on a joyride. Steve reveals during the ride that he has disabled the inertial dampeners and gives Shepard a taste of flight without mass effect fields, something which was commonplace before the advent of mass effect technology. If they are involved in a romance, Shepard can choose to hold hands and then cuddle in the back of the Kodiak while it flies on autopilot. Cortez can also be invited up to Shepard's apartment, along with James Vega, before or after the party. He will send an e\-mail asking for an invitation, if Shepard has helped him reach a sense of closure on his husband's death. He will wish to watch the biotiball game featuring the Seattle Sorcerers taking on the Usaru Maestros. Both Cortez and Vega will state their cases for each team to win. Shepard will be asked to back a team. Selecting a particular team will result in the supporter of that team winning the bet (though the Sorcerers always win the game). When Shepard questions this, the winner reveals that the bet was only on whether the Commander would be correct in their pick, rather than who would actually win. After the game, both of them thank Shepard and leave the apartment. If Cortez is romanced, James will tell them to enjoy their evening and leave the two of them to cuddle on the couch. Cortez can be invited to the party. In the beginning, he hangs out with James, Ashley/Kaidan and Jack (if they're present). Cortez thanks Shepard for throwing the party and bringing everyone together. If the party setting was chosen to be energetic by Shepard, sometime later, Cortez is at the bar with Joker along with by Garrus, Javik, and Wrex (if they're present). Cortez gets into an argument with Joker regarding their choices of planets most harsh to life. He shows an interest in Prothean fighter craft which he discusses with Javik. At this point, Cortez gets into another argument with Joker regarding the latter's lack of gun training. Cortez insists on taking Joker to the shooting range while Joker insists that he doesn't need to because of EDI. Shepard can either support Joker or Cortez. If Shepard supports Cortez, Joker will agree to go to a gun range to practice, conditional on Cortez beating him in a drinking match. However, Joker's alcoholic concoction (a combination of "horse choker" and mouthwash) leads Cortez to surrender. If Shepard supports Joker, the argument ends. Later, if the party is energetic, Cortez starts dancing with a few friends. He applauds the Commander if they step into dance and comments its nice to see Shepard relaxing once in a while. He is the only person in that group who doesn't tease Shepard about their dancing style.
Steve Cortez drinks mescal late into the nights if he chooses to loosen up, although he relates to James Vega that he'd rather have some tequila.

Once the evacuation of Grissom Academy is completed and if Jack was present, Vega speaks appreciatively of her, saying that she is a tough woman, then adds that she is "hot." Vega also comments on the relationship between Anderson and Kahlee Sanders, saying that they make a nice couple. He speaks of his dad having a surname of "Sanders", clarifying that he and Kahlee are not related. After the krogan female's retrieval from Sur'Kesh, if Wrex was present, Vega admires Wrex for his tough guy attitude and is interested in hearing some of the old krogan's stories. If Mordin was also present, Vega finds his habit of speaking very fast quite funny, saying that "Mordin's mouth moves faster than a frog on a hot rock in the middle of summer." If Padok Wiks is present, Vega says that he finds the salarian to be be very strange, even compared to other salarians. Upon completing the investigation into rachni on Utukku, James shakes his head in amazement at Shepard's ability to find trouble. If Grunt was present, James quips that he is crazier than Shepard, but Shepard is better looking. After rescuing a turian platoon from Tuchanka, Vega compares the deserts there with those back on Earth, saying that the lizards and the worms are bigger on Tuchanka. He also remarks that the Primarch's son is in over his head. Once the Cerberus bomb was defused at the cost of Tarquin Victus' life, Vega sadly states that he would have liked to know Tarquin better. After the mission to cure the genophage, Vega comically asks Shepard if the cure they dispersed could affect them, lest they suddenly start growing scales. He also hopes that they can put aside the diplomacy and go back to fighting the Reapers. James occasionally chats with Cortez while off duty. At one time, he debates with Cortez on the topic: M35 Mako vs M44 Hammerhead. James asserts that the Mako is vastly superior to the Hammerhead, with its powerful cannon and durable armor triumphing over the Hammerhead's inability to take hits. Cortez disagrees, saying the Hammerhead's mobility and maneuverability more than makes up for its low durability. When James says that the Mako doesn't need mobility owing to the presence of a very powerful cannon, Cortez laughs and sarcastically suggests that the M29 Grizzly is more suitable for James. James immediately says that he loves that tank, leading to a snort from Cortez and a remark that only James would like grizzly bears. Yet another time, James congratulates Cortez for "loosening up" a little. When Cortez expresses misgivings over drinking mescal late into the night, James says that it gives one heart which is needed to fight the war. Cortez disagrees, saying it would give him heartburn and moans about not finding decent tequila. James suggests Cortez should be responsible for setting up drinks as a procurement specialist and asks him to set the up. After stopping Udina's coup on the Citadel, James reveals that he knew Udina was a dirty bastard, but never guessed the Councilor was that rotten. After giving his thoughts on Udina to Shepard, he complains about people not seeing that they have to work together if they are going to win the fight against the Reapers, but Shepard tells him that when people are scared they are slow to trust. James agrees but also states he's adopting a 'shoot first, ask questions later' policy when dealing with politicians. Shepard finds that fair enough. Eventually, Vega asks to speak to Shepard privately. After Shepard invites Vega to the Captain's Cabin using the intercom, Vega explains he has been approached with an offer from the Systems Alliance to undergo N7 training. However, Vega is unsure whether or not to accept the offer since N7 training is a lot of work, and Vega humbly wonders why he was even approached, given his past failure, hence the private conversation. He also confesses that during that mission, his team was betrayed by a colonist who was actually a Cerberus spy working with the Collectors. Vega had no choice but to kill the spy and destroy the Collector ship, which left himself, a civilian, and one other squad member as the sole survivors of the mission. Shepard can either encourage Vega to go for it without hesitation or tell him that a decision such like that is one only he can make. James asks the Commander to refrain from mentioning his current situation to anyone. Shepard accepts, and James thanks them. James announces his intent to go back to the hangar, claiming that things are too soft around Shepard's cabin, though Shepard says the bed is much harder than it looks.

- According to Dusty Everman, early designs of Cortez gave him a lighter skin color, which was why many of his scenes are darkly lit, as there was not enough time to adjust them to his final skin tone. Casey Hudson picked the final design of the character. - According to Mark Meer, he recorded many variations for Shepard's reaction to Cortez's death, depending on how much the player interacts with him. However, the game only used the "STEEVE!" recording, which was meant to be only heard if Cortez actually died and Shepard romanced him. - Cortez uses Incinerate during battles in the Mass Effect 3: Citadel mission Citadel Archives: Escape. - Cortez has mission\-related comments in the Normandy shuttle bay after completing the various "N7" Galaxy at War missions when the primary squadmates do not, though James Vega frequently chimes in. ##

James Vega talks to Shepard over comms saying he is coming to assist when the Spectre is being pursued by CAT6 mercenaries. If Urdnot Wrex is not alive, James Vega appears instead and fires a Cobra Missile Launcher at the C\-Sec shuttle carrying CAT6 troops, then supports Shepard and their ally as they fend off more CAT6 forces. James sends Shepard an email sometime after the incident requesting face time in the personal apartment. If Shepard invites him over, James initially starts with giving his opinion on the apartment, steering the conversation to romantic relationships and claiming he stopped fraternizing before he joined the military. Vega expresses interest in the Commander's "personal life", particularly with potential shipmate paramours, and adjusts his inquiries as much. Due to all the flirty banter between a female Shepard and James he says he can't really tell if the Commander is just yanking his chain, and Shepard may reply indicating she's actually interested or confirm she's just keeping him on his toes. If Shepard already has someone else, Vega instead asks if he's getting in the way between Shepard and her current love, and the Commander assures him he's not. If Shepard is in a relationship with either Garrus or Tali, James voices curiosity on the pairing, asking in particular about differences in "anatomy". Too awkward a topic, he just withdraws the question, claiming he doesn't really want to know. Vega also approves of a Shepard/Steve relationship, saying that although he likes to give Esteban a hard time the shuttle pilot is still a great guy who has been through a lot. With Shepard's goading, James finally states his purpose on dropping by: he takes off his shirt to show off his N7 tattoo. Regardless of Shepard's gender or romantic entanglements, James reaffirms his commitment to the mission, and takes his leave claiming Esteban needs his help working on the Normandy's shuttle. As James turns to leave, he discovers the punching bag in the lower bedroom and tells the Commander that they've been holding out on him, proceeding to exercise on the punching bag. Shepard can then interact with the bar between the bedroom and closet, and in doing so, may choose to perform a pull\-up. If so, James comments that his record is 182, and challenges the Commander to beat it. If not, James will either ask about a mulligan or else state that he saw Shepard do nothing. If Shepard accepts James's challenge, James comments on his CO's performance at certain landmarks, i.e. 10, 20, 50, 91 (half his record), 100 and around 110 (where he states most people would be happy with 100\). If the Commander does beat Vega's record, he's so amazed he is at a loss for words and merely asks how Shepard is doing. If Shepard feels they can do another round, James scoffs and defers to their judgement. If Shepard admits to needing help putting on armor next time, James' reaction has a few variations: he's eager to help on a female Shepard who allowed to call her "Lola", he feels the male Shepard earned the nickname "Loco" for the stunt, and if neither of these James deems the stunt itself loco. Regardless of the circumstances, Vega tells Shepard that they still got it, and advises not to let anyone tell them otherwise. Should Shepard fail more than twice to do a significant number of pullups, James will instead marvel at having seen something that Shepard isn't good at. While on shore leave, James also spends his time plying Silversun Strip's many diversions, like combat\-oriented games on Castle Arcade or Armax Arsenal Arena. Shepard may even take him along as a squad member for the latter if the Spectre wishes it. If Shepard is female and in a relationship with Garrus, James turns up in the upper bar of Silver Coast Casino, loitering by the kiosk when two familiar figures start dominating the dance floor. A small crowd gathers watching Shepard and Vakarian do the tango, James among them, and he expresses sly amusement when Shepard swings by in front of him. Shepard can invite Vega and Cortez for a night of drinks and watching biotiball featuring the Seattle Sorcerers taking on the Usaru Maestros, before or after the party. Cortez sends an e\-mail asking for an invitation, if Shepard has helped him reach a sense of closure on his husband's death. Both Cortez and Vega state their cases for each team to win. Vega backs the Maestros and is teased by Cortez for it, who cites Vega's support of the Maestros is mostly due to their players being beautiful asari, than their actual skill. Vega sheepishly admits he has got the "hots" for the Maestro players. Shepard is asked to back a team.

evidence.page: The SSV Normandy SR-2 (Part 4) — The Alliance Refit
evidence.text: Contains the armory, cargo hold, and two Kodiak shuttles. James Vega and Lieutenant Steve Cortez spend their time here. A procurement terminal sells equipment from various retailers at a slight premium over Citadel prices; a weapon modification bench, an armor locker, and a small gym are also here.

The Party at Shepard's Apartment. 2186, Citadel shore leave, after the clone was stopped and the Normandy retaken, before Cronos Station Shepard's personal apartment on the Wards — two floors, kitchen, bar by the window, poker den, balcony, hot tub, rock garden Joker, EDI, Liara, James Vega, Steve Cortez and Samantha Traynor are automatic. Everyone else is an optional invite, and only surviving squadmates whose Mass Effect 3 arcs are finished can come at all.

Lieutenant Steve Cortez was an Alliance pilot aboard the Normandy SR-2 in 2186, flying the UT-47A Kodiak that carried Commander Shepard and squad to missions, and a potential romance option for a male Shepard. An only child who lost both parents years earlier, Cortez had a husband, Robert, who was killed when the Collectors abducted the colony of Ferris Fields in 2185; Robert phoned Steve during the attack to tell him to escape and let him go. Steve kept a recording of the call and grieved heavily. He had served in the Alliance since around 2176, first in the First Fleet aboard the SSV Hawking flying F-61 Tridents, and five months before the Reaper invasion joined the Normandy SR-2 retrofit team, moving the armory to the shuttle bay.

Aboard the Normandy, Cortez maintained the armory alongside Lt. James Vega, an old friend from Fehl Prime, and preferred to keep busy to avoid thinking about Robert. Shepard could persuade him to take shore leave on the Citadel; he later visited the refugees' Memorial Wall to say goodbye to Robert and began to move on, reconnecting with old pilot friends and forwarding their information to Admiral Hackett to give the Alliance more pilots. A meeting at Purgatory could begin a relationship with a male Shepard or reinforce their friendship.

During the final assault on Earth, Cortez's shuttle was shot down by a Harvester after dropping off the squad. If he had visited the Memorial Wall he survived the crash and could be contacted by hologram; otherwise he died and Vega confirmed it, and his name appeared on the Normandy's memorial wall as "Steven Cortez." In the Leviathan DLC he crash-landed the shuttle and devised the plan for Shepard to reach Leviathan using a Triton mech. In the Citadel DLC he provided suppressive fire during the Spectre Archives infiltration, flew a skycar with Joker to block the hijacked Normandy from jumping to FTL, delivered a restrained Maya Brooks, and could take Shepard on a joyride in the Kodiak with the inertial dampeners disabled. If the Crucible was activated and the Reapers were controlled or Synthesis was chosen, Cortez placed Shepard's name on the memorial wall.

Besides being a Kodiak pilot aboard the Normandy SR\-2, Steve is also responsible for maintaining the Normandy's armory, a duty he shares with Lt. James Vega. Cortez and Vega are friends, having served together before on Fehl Prime. In between missions, they engage in off duty conversations. Cortez prefers to have as little time off from his duties as possible, since any time spent not working gives him too much time to think about Robert. Shepard has the option of convincing Cortez to take time off to leave the ship and succeeds. At first, Steve just loiters near the Normandy's docking bay on the Citadel, but he finds Shepard's suggestion a good idea since the vista of so many ships in flight brings him comfort and gets him thinking. He later visits the Memorial Wall for victims of Collector and Reaper attacks at the refugee docks, where Shepard can once more offer words of support. The downtime helps him to move on, and he meets up with some old pilot friends and forwards their information to Admiral Hackett, giving the Alliance some much needed pilots. A further encounter at Purgatory allows a male Shepard to begin a relationship with him, or reinforces their friendship otherwise. During the final assault on Earth, after dropping off Shepard's squad, Cortez's shuttle is shot down by a Harvester. If he has been persuaded to visit the Memorial Wall, he survives the crash and can be contacted via hologram later. Steve is later present in front of the Normandy's memorial wall with the rest of Shepard's surviving crew if the Crucible was activated, paying his respects to the dead. If Steve was never interacted with much, he dies when his shuttle gets shot during the final assault on Earth. He cannot be contacted and James confirms Cortez's death. Much later, if Shepard uses the Crucible, Steve's name is listed on the Normandy's memorial wall as "Steven Cortez".

This page catalogs in-universe forms of recreation across the Milky Way and Andromeda: films, plays, books, magazines, musical acts, sports, and games. Notable theatrical works included Francis Kitt's award-winning all-elcor production of Hamlet, which ran over 14 hours and used elcor body language and pheromones, and his planned Macbeth with a krogan lead and a live pyjak; the elcor doctor Yorrik authored an unproduced 16-hour all-elcor Macbeth but died before reaching Andromeda. Starless (2173) was a gothic horror masterpiece whose vacuum-preserved sets on airless Faringor became a tourist draw.

The Blasto franchise followed the galaxy's first hanar Spectre through many films, including Blasto: the Jellyfish Stings, Blasto Saves Christmas, Blasto 6: Partners in Crime, and Blasto 7: Blasto Goes to War! (co-starring Shepard and Javik). Blasto lines quoted include: "This one doesn't have time for your solid waste excretions." / "This one has forgotten whether its heatsink is over capacity. It wonders whether the criminal scum considers itself fortunate?" / "Enkindle THIS."

Citadel, directed by Risa Uvarsen, dramatized Shepard's role in the Eden Prime War, with a scene varying by whether Shepard saved the Council. Fleet and Flotilla was an award-winning vid praised for its positive turian-quarian romance; Shepard and Tali could watch it during Citadel shore leave. Its quoted lines: Bellicus, "But Shalei. We can never be together. I have my duty, and you, have your people." / Shalei, "Not tonight. Tonight, I'm as free as the dust in the solar wind." / Shalei, "I want you to see behind this mask. I want you to see who I truly am." / Bellicus, "I already have." Last of the Legion was a turian war film watched aboard the Tempest, quoted: Jorax Halabrian, "I never left the Legion. It left me. But I know my duty." Nekyia Corridor was a record-breaking human simstim that outgrossed the asari classic Confederates.

Dozens of other films are listed via Cerberus Daily News box-office reports, including Blue Steel, Vaenia, and the "Taetrus effect" comedies. Games covered include Chess (popular with elcor; General Oleg Petrovsky's holographic board passes to Shepard if Omega is liberated), Kepesh-Yakshi, Galaxy of Fantasy, Quasar, Skillian Five poker, and Three-Card-Monte. Publications include Fornax ("the galaxy's finest xenophilia"), Ascension and Revelation by Drew Karpyshyn, and Justicar Heroes. Sports include biotiball, clawball, kailat ring-ball, the krogan sport kowla, and Armax Arsenal Arena combat simulators.

April was a colonist on Fehl Prime in 2185 and the daughter of Christine. She was a lively little girl who idolized the Systems Alliance Marines and worshipped Lieutenant James Vega in particular, their relationship almost like that of brother and sister. She sometimes pretended to be a marine by putting on James's combat helmet.

During the installation of the colony's defense cannon, April came to meet Vega with her mother, snapped him a military salute, and pretended to be a professional. Vega gave her a badge to wear. She teased Vega about looking at Treeya differently from others; Vega deflected by hoisting her onto his shoulders and telling her to act as a lookout for bad guys, which she happily did, imagining herself an Alliance private. When she asked about the large gun the Alliance had installed, Vega promised her he would use it to keep the colony safe.

When the Collectors attacked the colony, April and Christine were paralyzed by the Seeker Swarms, and Delta Squad was forced to watch as the Collectors carried them away to their ship. Later, after Delta Squad infiltrated the Collector ship and released the antidote from the processing plant, April reawakened along with the other colonists. She never gave up hope in Vega, and contacted him over the comm using Toni's omni-tool, telling him to come and save them and that she would always believe in him. Vega then had to make a difficult choice, and the one he made caused the death of April and the other colonists when the Collector ship crashed onto the planet's surface before the colonists could be evacuated.

codex.text: - Abrudas: turian lieutenant who served in the First Contact War in 2157 under General Desolas Arterius; her soldiers found a downed turian research vessel crashed on Shanxi, and acting on a false message from Desolas she led a squad into a trap and unwittingly gave human mercenaries the vessel's location. The first female turian visually depicted in the franchise. (source: Abrudas)

- Ashley Williams was granddaughter of General Williams, who surrendered the garrison at Shanxi to the turians in the First Contact War, becoming the first human to surrender to an alien force; the resulting "Williams curse" stalled her Alliance career. (source: Ashley Williams)

- The First Contact War (2157) began when turians attacked a human fleet activating a dormant relay and occupied Shanxi; Admiral Kastanie Drescher's Second Fleet retook it and the Council brokered peace, making the Systems Alliance humanity's governing body (source: Human)

- The First Contact War (2157) began when a human scout fleet activating a dormant mass relay met a turian patrol; the turians invaded Shanxi, the Alliance took control of the human response, and the roughly three-month conflict cost 623 human lives before the Citadel Council brokered peace. (source: Systems Alliance)

- The First Contact War (2157) began when a turian patrol fleet destroyed an Alliance expedition at the Shanxi-Theta relay; the turians then captured Shanxi after a guerrilla siege in which they dropped orbital debris to level city blocks and starve out marine fire teams, forcing the garrison to surrender (source: Shanxi).

- The First Contact War, called the Relay 314 Incident by the turians, was a three-month 2157 conflict that began when turian patrols fired on humans reactivating the dormant Relay 314, an act forbidden since the Rachni Wars. The turians besieged and took the colony Shanxi until General Williams surrendered it; a month later Admiral Kastanie Drescher's Second Fleet retook the world and the Council brokered peace. Only 623 humans died, but the war fixed humanity's reputation as aggressors, fed Alliance xenophobia and the rise of Terra Firma and Cerberus, and left Saren Arterius with a lasting hatred of humanity after his brother's death. (source: First Contact War)

- Without Arcturus Station the Alliance could not have fielded the task force that liberated Shanxi and forced the Turian Hierarchy to negotiate during the Relay 314 Incident (First Contact War). (source: Arcturus Station)
